basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 28.' and it opens 'Vers. 28.-- Sed Israel erit nomen tuum. Mutatio nominis benedictio fuit. Israel autem,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 28.-- Sed Israel erit nomen tuum. Mutatio nominis benedictio fuit. Israel autem, quamvis bene | ab omnibus vir videns Deum interpretari dicatur, melius princeps cum Deo dicitur. Et est sensus: Nequaquam ultra vocaberis Jacob, sed Israel erit nomen tuum, id est, sicut ego princeps sum, sic et tu, qui mecum luctari potuisti.
